hero.p1: Classroom activities that build the thinking the Student Success Tool will ask for — explaining, connecting evidence, and applying ideas to new situations.
hero.p2: Not another stack of test-prep packets. These are short, reusable routines you can drop into instruction you already teach, with teacher look-fors that tell you what to do next.
hero.note: No login. No student data is collected or transmitted. Everything runs in the browser.
sec.sub: More SST activity sets are planned. This page will grow as they are released.
card.ace.alt: ACE the SST: Deeper Thinking in Elementary Science. Four elementary students observe a bowl of warm water with a thermometer, beside circles labeled A Articulate, C Connect, E Extend.
card.ace.p: Paired entry and exit tickets built on the ACE framework: Articulate, Connect, Extend. Filter by grade and SST science strand, flip between student and teacher views, and score the response with a SOLO guide that names the next instructional move.
card.soon.p: Additional sets are planned for other grade bands and content areas, following the same pattern: a short thinking routine, a teacher look-for, and a scoring guide that points to the next move. Check back as they are released.
about.p1: Beginning in 2027–2028, the Student Success Tool (SST) replaces STAAR in Texas with beginning-, middle-, and end-of-year assessments. TEA’s draft elementary science blueprints organize questions around four strands — Matter and Energy; Force, Motion, and Energy; Earth and Space; and Organisms and Environments — using multiple choice, multiselect, multipart, and inline choice formats.
about.p2: Formats change; the thinking underneath does not. A student who can only recall a definition stalls the moment a question changes one condition. The activities here are designed around that gap:
about.li1: Articulate — explain what happened in your own words.
about.li2: Connect — tie the evidence to the underlying concept.
about.li3: Extend — predict what changes when one condition changes.
about.p3: Score what students say with a five-level SOLO guide, then teach from the level they actually show you. Full details on the assessment design are in TEA’s House Bill 8 student assessment resources.
f.disclaimer: Independent classroom resources aligned to the draft SST blueprints and the current assessed curriculum. Not official TEA assessments.
